title: Seeds with Unusual Tickets
fact_notes: オリジナル論説。一般的原理と架空の例を用いた教材であり、架空例は実在の調査結果・史料・実験結果ではない。制作台帳は来歴確認用。

sentences.en: A seed that falls directly beneath its parent plant may land in a place already occupied by leaves, roots, and other young plants.
sentences.ja: 親植物の真下に落ちる種は、葉や根や他の若い植物がすでに場所を占めている所に落ちるかもしれない。

sentences.en: Plants cannot walk away from crowded surroundings, but the structures surrounding their seeds can help those seeds travel.
sentences.ja: 植物は混んだ環境から歩いて離れられないが、種を包む構造によって種が移動できることがある。

sentences.en: Different forms of dispersal connect the lives of plants with moving air, flowing water, and the activities of animals.
sentences.ja: 異なる散布の形は植物の生命を動く空気、流れる水、動物の活動と結びつける。

sentences.en: These connections become easier to appreciate when we compare the physical features of several familiar kinds of seeds.
sentences.ja: 身近な数種類の種の物理的特徴を比較すると、こうしたつながりを理解しやすくなる。

sentences.en: A light seed equipped with a broad, thin structure may remain in the air longer than a compact seed of similar mass.
sentences.ja: 広く薄い構造を持つ軽い種は、同程度の質量の小さくまとまった種より長く空中にとどまり得る。

sentences.en: A fruit with a surface suited to floating may travel along a stream before reaching a bank where conditions permit growth.
sentences.ja: 浮くのに適した表面の果実は、生長を許す条件がある岸に到達する前に小川を移動し得る。

sentences.en: Other plants produce fruits that attract animals, which may carry seeds to locations far from the parent plant.
sentences.ja: 別の植物は動物を引き寄せる果実を作り、動物は種を親植物から遠い場所へ運ぶことがある。

sentences.en: However, a useful structure does not guarantee that every individual seed will arrive at a suitable destination.
sentences.ja: しかし有用な構造は全ての個別の種が適切な目的地に到着することを保証しない。

sentences.en: Imagine a classroom model in which students drop paper shapes from the same height above a marked surface.
sentences.ja: 生徒が印をつけた面の上の同じ高さから紙の形を落とす教室模型を想像しよう。

sentences.en: They could compare how the shapes descend, or introduce a gentle current of air and observe how far each travels.
sentences.ja: 形がどう下降するか比較したり、穏やかな気流を加えてそれぞれの移動距離を観察したりできる。

sentences.en: The model would illustrate selected effects of shape without reproducing the biological characteristics of real seeds.
sentences.ja: 模型は本物の種の生物学的特徴を再現せず、形の特定の影響を例示するものだろう。

sentences.en: Its results would therefore need to be interpreted within the limits of the activity.
sentences.ja: したがって結果は活動の限界内で解釈する必要がある。

sentences.en: Dispersal alone is not sufficient to establish a new plant.
sentences.ja: 散布だけでは新しい植物が定着するには十分ではない。

sentences.en: A seed that reaches distant ground may encounter insufficient moisture, unsuitable temperatures, or competition from existing vegetation.
sentences.ja: 遠い地面に到達した種は不十分な水分、不適切な温度、既存植生との競争に直面し得る。

sentences.en: The ability to move and the ability to survive after movement are consequently related but distinct challenges.
sentences.ja: 移動する能力と移動後に生存する能力は、したがって関連するが別個の課題だ。

sentences.en: Studying only the distance traveled would leave important questions about the plant's life cycle unanswered.
sentences.ja: 移動距離だけを調べると植物の生活環について重要な問いが未解決のままになる。

sentences.en: Even a seed that arrives in an apparently suitable place may need to wait until conditions allow germination.
sentences.ja: 一見適切な場所に着いた種でさえ、発芽できる条件になるまで待つ必要がある場合がある。

sentences.en: A seed is both a product of a living organism and a potential beginning of another one.
sentences.ja: 種は生物の産物であると同時に別の生物の始まりとなる可能性を持つ。

sentences.en: Its features can influence the opportunities available for reaching a new environment.
sentences.ja: 特徴は新環境に到達するための機会に影響し得る。

sentences.en: Nevertheless, the outcome also depends on relationships with the surroundings that the seed eventually encounters.
sentences.ja: それでも結果は種が最終的に遭遇する環境との関係にも依存する。

sentences.en: The seemingly simple act of dispersal reminds us that survival involves much more than the properties of a single organism.
sentences.ja: 一見単純な散布は生存が一個体の特性以上のことを伴うと気づかせる。

questions.prompt: Why may remaining beneath the parent plant be disadvantageous?
options: The parent plant always destroys its seeds.
Seeds can grow only in water.
Every seed needs to remain in the air.
Other plants may already occupy the space and resources.
questions.explanation_ja: 既存の植物との競争があり得る。

questions.prompt: Which moving things can contribute to dispersal?
What can a broad, thin structure help a seed do?
options: Sink more rapidly in a stream.

questions.prompt: Why does a useful structure not guarantee success?
options: Every seed has exactly the same structure.
Seeds cannot be transported by animals.
Transport does not ensure arrival under suitable conditions.
questions.explanation_ja: 適切な到達環境は保証されない。

questions.prompt: What could students compare in the model?
options: The growth rates of actual trees.
The descent and travel of paper shapes.
The exact weight of every seed species.

questions.prompt: Why limit conclusions from the model?
options: It reproduces every feature of real plants.
It measures only the students' opinions.
It illustrates selected physical effects rather than all biological features.
questions.explanation_ja: 生物学的特徴は再現しない。

questions.prompt: What problems might a distant seed face?
options: An absence of all surrounding plants.
A complete lack of movement before arrival.
questions.explanation_ja: 水分・温度・競争など。

questions.prompt: Why is distance alone insufficient as a measure?
options: Survival after arrival is a separate challenge.
The movement of seeds has no biological importance.
Distance cannot be measured in a model.

questions.prompt: What does potential mean in this context?
Which statement best expresses the argument?
options: All seeds must travel as far as possible.
A single paper model explains every species.
Seed dispersal depends on structures and environmental relationships, and movement alone does not ensure survival.
Seed survival depends exclusively on seed mass.
questions.explanation_ja: 構造・環境・生存の関係。

grammar.explanation_ja: sufficient to doは〜するのに十分。
